baseline_measurements.description: baseline-repro-p50, 384x640, own val-selected thresholds. PyTorch CPU on Mac vexcalibur; native package-default fp32/fp16 on xcng0. Primary comparison uses native fp16, matching the provisional export. Small-object recall is zero for all three baseline seeds.

aspect_ratio.label: measured
aspect_ratio.bucket_boundaries: portrait <1; square [1,1.1547); 4:3 [1.1547,1.5396); approx-16:9 >=1.5396, includes wider images
aspect_ratio.small_definition: WS1 projected short side <32 px; fixed cohort uses 800x800 for both
aspect_ratio.threshold_policy: subset R@P90 is diagnostic; no operating threshold or promotion gate changes
aspect_ratio.interpretation: The geometry hypothesis is supported for this checkpoint. Square-to-rectangular content scale is 0.56 in portrait and square images, versus a pigeon-weighted 0.957 in the wide bucket. At the respective full-test P90 cuts, 38 of 39 lost matches are portrait pigeons, one is in the 4:3 bucket, and square/wide matches are unchanged. The fixed square-defined small cohort also loses recall, so this is more than a changing small-object denominator. It is an observational geometry comparison, not a controlled attribution of every error: canvas padding and sampling also change. The wide bucket contains only two positive images and 17 boxes, so unchanged recall does not establish real-camera performance. The square CPU result is 0.8017 for this seed; the approximately 0.78 WS5 value is a three-seed mean. Checked-in app/config.yaml and CameraConfig still default to 640x480. The scale-match argument requires an actual 16:9 capture stream; WS10 should verify the deployed stream geometry. No capture setting was changed.
